content.content:
78-| Sessions Recycle Bin | a soft-deleted project-less "session" row lands in a top-level `Recycle Bin` subsection under the Sessions header (revealed from its right-click menu, hidden + collapsed by default) — the session twin of `(SESSION-LIFECYCLE)`. Deleted sessions used to fall into a void: the bucket classifier moved them out of the active lane, but the only surface that rendered a soft-deleted row was the per-project bin and a session has no project row, so the X on a session was an unrecoverable disappearance. The deleted bucket is now partitioned by session-ness the same way snoozed/archived are; the session rows sort by `deletedAt` DESC, honour the same retention display window + "Show all" toggle, and carry per-row Restore and context-menu Restore / Delete permanently. Reveal + collapse flags ride the fixed-size `v2UserPreferences` singleton (no per-entity key), and `deleteWorkspace` accepts an EXPLICIT null projectId so a session with no local-state row soft-deletes instead of being refused | `(RECYCLE-BIN-SESSIONS)` |
79-| Auto-resume stuck chats | when a Claude chat dies on an API failure the JSONL watcher classifies it (deny-list-first: rate-limit-with-reset-time / transient-rate-limit / server-error / connection-drop / half-stop are resumable; auth/policy/bad-image/model-unavailable are notify-only) after a finality/quiescence gate, and a durable MAIN-side registry auto-sends "resume from exactly where everything was left" — fire-at-parsed-reset-time (+30s, DST-correct, fire-now-if-already-past, ≤8d sane cap) for usage limits, else a 60s→×3 backoff capped at 5 sends / 24h. Every send is gated at fire time (toggle on, still the last meaningful transcript line, host-service `commandRunning`=idle + agent-session binding match) so it can never auto-confirm a menu, land mid-turn, or run at a bare shell. Any trusted interaction with that terminal cancels (persisted tombstone survives reload/restart). Account-wide cohorts are jittered + concurrency-capped. Global toggle (default on). Claude-only in v1 — Codex auto-resume is deferred (the on-disk corpus has no validated standalone usage-limit signal). Dots untouched (separate IPC variant + toasts) | `(AUTO-RESUME)`, `autoResumeManager`, `writeInputIfIdleSession`, `useAutoResumeActivity`, `AutoResumeController` |
80-| Dot-decision log + codex pid-reuse cap | superset-notify.py writes an always-on bounded `~/.superset/logs/dot-decisions.log` line at each terminal turn-end decision (the POSTed eventType + WHY a hold won — codex job / background_tasks / subagent markers / GREEN / BLUE / RED), and `_codex_job_active` age-caps pid-bearing `running` codex job records at 6h so a recycled PID can't pin the dot yellow forever (a cap-skipped stale record is logged, so a premature-green is auditable) | `_decision_log` |
81-| Idle/zombie teammate hold reaped | an agent set Claude Code still reports `running` in background_tasks[] but that has produced NO activity (SubagentStart / subagent-scoped PostToolUse refresh a `.bgactive` timer) for 15 min stops pinning the lead's dot yellow — the harness never flips an idle long-lived teammate (or one that died without a clean SubagentStop) to a finished status, so the hold previously lasted until the team was disbanded / the session ended. The JSONL watcher re-asserts yellow if a reaped set is in fact still writing. A stale reap of a MIXED set no longer greens live work: `_split_background` tracks live `type:"shell"` entries separately, so zombie agents + running background shells resolve to the blue shell remainder (live 2026-07-21 incident: two running crash/build monitors showed no dot after the zombie-teammate hold staled out); an agent-only zombie set still greens | `(BG-STALE)` |
82:| Idle teammates green deterministically | Claude Code reports finished teammates in the Stop payload's background_tasks[] as `status:"running"` FOREVER (captured live: 33 teammate entries, all "running", for a session whose 44 teammates had all finished hours earlier) — and the (BG-STALE) reap only runs inside hook events, so a session whose LAST event landed while the set was <15 min idle latched yellow indefinitely (nothing ever re-evaluated; 9 terminals observed stuck). superset-notify.py now keeps a per-terminal teammate LEDGER parsed incrementally from the lead session transcript (payload `transcript_path`; offset+state cached in `<terminalId>.teamstate.json`, keyed by transcript path so /resume self-invalidates): Agent-spawn / SendMessage-wake / non-idle teammate- or agent-messages mark a name active, an `idle_notification` teammate-message marks it idle. At Stop/SubagentStop, when EVERY tracked teammate is provably idle, unfinished teammate-type entries are dropped BEFORE the split/snapshot/hold decision — the lead greens (or blues on a shell remainder) at its actual final turn end instead of holding forever. Positive proof only: no transcript / no teammates seen / any parse error / any teammate not idle → entries kept (old behaviour + (BG-STALE) unchanged behind it); raw fork agentIds ("a"+hex) are excluded from the predicate (forks have real hook lifecycles and would never idle-notify) — and NAMED forks are excluded too: the spawn parser reads the Agent tool-use input's `subagent_type`, skips tracking fork spawns regardless of name, and indexes them by tool-use-id so their completed task-notification untracks exactly that spawn (a named fork previously latched "active" forever and made the all-idle predicate unsatisfiable — live 2026-07-21); cache schema v2 forces one full rescan to self-heal already-poisoned ledgers; subagent/workflow/shell entries always pass through untouched; bg_ids marker reconciliation still uses the RAW list. Decision log carries a `[teammate-idle: dropped N ...]` suffix for auditability. (TEAM-ENTRY-MATCH, 2026-07-22): the all-idle predicate proved unsatisfiable in real multi-agent sessions — 55 permanently-"active" ledger names (named non-fork Agent spawns like sol/general-purpose/review agents that finish via task-notification and never idle-notify, forks re-marked active by a later SendMessage, and "name [hash]" duplicate-suffix splits) held 25 finished wrangler teammates yellow all day. 84-| Nightly dependency-consistency + lock regen | the nightly merge can introduce dependency-state drift that only the build discovers (after a windows-arm64 runner spins up): a stale fork root `overrides` entry that pins a package to a version different from the merged workspace pin (electron-builder "production dependency not found …"), or a `bun.lock` left stale by an upstream package.json bump (frozen-install fails). The merge now runs an override-consistency gate (fails loud on any exact override↔pin mismatch) + regenerates `bun.lock` to match the merged manifests with the build's exact bun version (which also fails loud, in the cheap merge job, if the merged manifests don't resolve or a pin is age-blocked) — so this class of build failure is caught/fixed before the windows-arm64 build spins up, baseline untouched on failure (recovery loop). No full `--frozen-lockfile` install runs here: the merge runner is linux, so a platform-specific install quirk would be a false abort, and the regenerated lock is consistent with the manifests by construction. The fork carries NO mastra `overrides` and pins `@mastra/core`/`mastracode` to upstream's exact versions in all three workspaces (upstream keeps mastra consistent via identical exact pins; the seed commit's redundant override + a recovery merge that resolved the pins DOWN to 0.18.0 were the recurring breakage, both corrected) | `(LOCK-REGEN)` |
85-| Fork-owned workflow dir | `.github/workflows/` carries ONLY the fork's own workflows — upstream CI files were dropped at fork creation (they target upstream's infra/secrets) and the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` can NEVER push a workflow-file change anyway (no `workflows` scope exists for it: "refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow"). Upstream desktop-v1.14.3 added `deploy-relay.yml`, which merged CLEANLY and then killed the candidate push after every gate had already passed. The nightly now deterministically restores the fork's exact workflow set mid-merge (`git checkout --no-overlay HEAD -- .github/workflows`) BEFORE conflict detection, so upstream workflow additions/edits never enter the fork, never reach the AI resolver, and never hit the push restriction — and the dropped upstream CI delta is SURFACED, not silently erased (job summary + log + handed to the semantic review, which appends advisory `CI-NOTE:` lines when upstream moves build-relevant logic into its CI), with a pre-commit postcondition proving the committed tree carries zero workflow-dir changes. Wanting an upstream workflow = deliberate local commit with a user token | `(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)` |
86-| Nightly pipeline integrity | three cheap deterministic guards on the merge→build→advance hand-offs: a fatal (non-conflict) `git merge` failure is caught via missing MERGE_HEAD instead of masquerading as a clean merge (the `set +e` wrapper accepts every nonzero exit); the build + advance jobs consume the merge commit's immutable SHA — not the mutable `nightly/*` branch name — under a workflow-level `concurrency` group (queue, never cancel), and advance refuses to fast-forward main if the candidate ref moved; `gh release create` tags the exact built commit via `--target` + a post-publish remote-tag assert (without `--target` gh tags the DEFAULT branch tip, which during a nightly is pre-advance main — every nightly-published release tag pointed one commit behind the installer's true source until 2026-07-11) | `(NIGHTLY-INTEGRITY)` |
87-| Companion keep-awake | the phone/watch companion is worthless if the desktop sleeps mid-question: the answer path lives in host-service, which dies with the machine. The main process holds a power-save blocker (and suppresses app-initiated sleep) for exactly as long as the companion bridge is enabled AND running AND at least one device is paired, released the moment any of the three stops being true — it never pins the machine awake unconditionally, and it never blocks display sleep (screen off is fine; suspend is not) | `(KEEP-AWAKE)` |

89-| Companion pairing surface (desktop) | the entry point the phone's own instructions name — "open Superset and choose 'Pair a device'" — without which the companion feature cannot be bootstrapped at all: `openPairing` is reachable only from the desktop's authenticated tRPC surface, so nothing else can ever open the one 120 s LAN window. A row in Experimental settings reads `companion.status` and derives its own availability (off / enabled-but-failed-to-start / running are three different messages, because they need three different actions from the user) rather than offering a button that can only fail; it opens a fork-only dialog that renders the returned URI as a QR and counts the window down. The pairing code lives in the URL FRAGMENT, so the dialog is the only thing that ever holds it: it is never logged (diagnostics use only the non-secret `pairingRef`), never persisted, never an attribute, never selectable text (a screenshot of a QR expires in 120 s; a screenshot of the string does not), and the flow component is unmounted on close so the value dies with the dialog. Dismissing takes the 0.0.0.0:47611 listener down instead of leaving it up for the rest of the window, and every window operation is serialised because the bridge allows exactly one process-wide (an unserialised close could land after a later open and silently kill the new window). States are honest and bounded — opening / open-with-time-remaining / expired / failed-with-the-server's-reason, never an unbounded spinner. It does NOT claim "paired": the bridge exposes no completion signal to the desktop, so the expiry copy points at the phone, which does know. QR is drawn by a dependency-free byte-mode encoder (level M, versions 1-40, full mask selection) — a QR library would move `package.json`/`bun.lock` under the `(LOCK-REGEN)` gate — always dark-on-white regardless of theme, since an inverted symbol is unreadable to some decoders | `(COMPANION-PAIRING-UI)`, `(COMPANION-PAIRING-ENTRY)`, `(COMPANION-PAIRING-SEARCH)` |
90-| Companion bridge (phone/watch) | fork-only host-service subsystem (`packages/host-service/src/companion/`) that lets a paired Android phone/watch read agent status and answer a blocked AskUserQuestion. Loopback listener on a fixed port behind a Cloudflare tunnel + Access service token, with the bridge validating the Access JWT itself and failing closed; every body is an end-to-end AES-256-GCM sealed envelope keyed on a per-device key that is DERIVED at pairing and never transmitted, with method/path/status/nonce bound into the AAD and a disk-persisted replay cache that outlives the freshness window. The client sends semantic intent only — questionId, fingerprint, option indices — so no wire field can express "send these bytes to that terminal"; the bridge owns the picker byte contract and injects the validated sequence inside ONE critical section holding the per-terminal lock in the same process as the pty writer, under an answer-wide lease. `(ANSWER-GUARDLESS)` means every pending captured Claude question with a terminal target is offered even before capability/session negotiation and even when sidebar curation hides its ordinary thread, and after fingerprint/shape validation, no transcript, screen, renderer, Windows login-session, agent-binding, permission-latch, marker, liveness or capability observation may veto or downgrade it; display-off and a Windows lock screen behave exactly like an unlocked desktop, and only daemon-acknowledged `pty.write` calls are counted as successful and confirmed; `(ANSWER-FRAME-PACING)` keeps protocol-v3 keystrokes as discrete frames with a fixed 500 ms settling gap after each acknowledged non-final frame (renewing the answer lease immediately before every following write), because a daemon acknowledgement precedes Claude's picker transition and burst N-question digits can land on the wrong item — measured on Claude Code 2.1.228 the boundary failure is a SILENTLY submitted wrong answer set (a 250 ms run misattributed every answer one question over), while 500 ms passed 3/3 plus a final clean shipping-value proof; the dynamic sequence deadline scales from the actual encoded frame count rather than duplicating the encoder's picker-shape limits, while protocol v2 remains one complete unpaced legacy frame with its honest durable `unconfirmed` fence; pacing observes no screen/renderer/transcript/display/lock/agent state and can never veto or downgrade an acknowledged write; that acknowledgement never prematurely hides the question — positive matching PostToolUse/tool-result evidence performs settlement/retraction, while a best-effort PTY resize nudge asks Claude to repaint its consumed picker without becoming a write veto or outcome downgrade (the daemon protocol version is bumped; a detached v2 daemon remains adoptable and still receives the ENTIRE encoded companion sequence in one ordered legacy input frame, but because it cannot acknowledge that write the bridge returns durable `unconfirmed`, marks the question stale and retains the duplicate fence rather than lying about confirmation, refusing on negotiated capability state or stopping after the first keystroke) (per-keystroke locking interleaves two multi-select answers into a third one neither device chose). First-answer-wins, zero write retries, read-the-outcome instead. Push is data-only opaque ids with runtime assertions that make text leakage throw — with ONE narrow, explicitly-waived exception since 2026-08-16: `(ALERT-CONTEXT-NAMES)` lets the project, workspace and tab names ride a v3 push in plaintext so an alert can say which chat it is about, while every other free string stays banned and the exempt key set is enumerated by a test; v1/v2 are frozen, keep their 160-byte leak tripwire, and still carry nothing but ids. Push is PRESENCE-GATED rather than delayed: a question buzzes IMMEDIATELY when the user is away from the desktop, and never while they are at it. Presence is two signals — human keystrokes into a terminal WebSocket (never the companion's own answer-injection path, or a phone answer would read as desk presence) and a 15 s Electron beacon carrying OS idle time plus lock state, with a locked screen overriding a recent keystroke. A held question is held with NO ceiling: it is cancelled if answered at the desk, and fired the moment presence lapses (walking away, locking, or the beacon going stale), with a 10 s settling window after a resume so a machine the user has just woken does not empty its queue into their wrist. Armed and sent states are rows in host.db, so a host-service restart neither loses a held push nor re-sends a sent one, and every send is serialised against its own retraction so a notification can never outlive its subject. Wire contract: `superset-companion/PROTOCOL.md`. The 24 h idempotency + status ledger is a TABLE in host.db, not a file, because the race it has to settle cannot be settled by a file: a status read can overtake an answer that was admitted but has not yet recorded itself, and absence then says nothing about whether it is about to be typed. `/v1/answer` and `/v1/answer/status` therefore race atomically for the right to decide — the answer compare-and-sets an `in_flight` claim BEFORE encoding or PTY injection begins, the status path compare-and-sets a `closed_not_received` tombstone that permanently forbids typing — and whichever wins, the loser is bound by it. Coverage is an opaque epoch the client echoes back and the server compares for equality, rotated transactionally with any prune, so no client-side clock arithmetic can manufacture a false "it was not sent"; the server returns one discriminated outcome and the client renders it rather than proving anything. Durability is asserted (`PRAGMA synchronous = FULL`) rather than inferred from NTFS rename ordering, and rows validate individually, so a corrupt row costs one requestId its status instead of quarantining every other record’s 24 hours. `(FREETEXT-N2-PROVEN)` widens WHERE a typed answer is accepted: free text now works on a multi-question prompt — 59% of real traffic — because the per-question sequence was driven in a pty and the agent's own `tool_result` confirmed it (the editor-closing `\r` ADVANCES to the next question rather than submitting, so a free-text question and a digit question compose and the prompt is submitted by the same review-screen return that already ends an all-digit N>1 answer). `(MSEL-N2-PROVEN)` closes the last prompt shape: a multi-select question inside an N>1 prompt is a per-question group of toggle digits terminated by the SAME right-arrow that submits a lone multi-select — there it ADVANCES (next question mid-prompt, review screen on the last) — driven first, middle and last, twice each, mixed with free-text siblings and with the zero-toggle empty group (which the CLI accepts and then OMITS from the `tool_result`, exactly as a desk submit past the review warning does). What the earlier refutation actually refuted was the N=1 submit PAIR reused verbatim: its trailing `\r` landed on the next question. The one shape still refused is refused on EVIDENCE rather than on caution: on a multi-select question the free-text row's digit toggles a checkbox, the body text is swallowed with no echo and the terminating `\r` toggles whatever row the caret was on — a run that asked for free text came back answered with the first option instead. A `\r` into a multi-select question is the single most dangerous byte this contract knows, so `assertNoReturnIntoMultiSelect` re-checks every emitted sequence against the prompt itself. The picker contract is per build AND per shape, and one build's proof can never backfill another's | `(COMPANION-BRIDGE)`, `(ANSWER-GUARDLESS)`, `(ANSWER-LEDGER)`, `(PUSH-PRESENCE)`, `(FREETEXT-N2-PROVEN)`, `(MSEL-N2-PROVEN)` |

# superset-windows-arm64 — Windows ARM64 fork maintenance

This repo is a **vendored fork** of [superset-sh/superset]: the full upstream
source with our Windows ARM64 + feature changes committed on top, plus CI that
builds a native **Windows ARM64** one-click NSIS installer. The fork is the
source of truth; we track upstream by **merging its deltas**, not by
re-applying changes. `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt` records the upstream
`desktop-v*` tag the baseline currently sits on.

## Setup / architecture (high level)

- **Build (deterministic steps, self-repairing).** `.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml`
  orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop `(BUILD-REPAIR)`: the actual build
  steps (install → compile → materialize the win-arm64 native closure
  (`scripts/materialize-native-closure.sh`: libsql/tokenizers/node-pty) →
  package the installer → verify packaged natives are ARM64 → publish) live in
  `.github/actions/arm64-build/action.yml` as thin shims over `scripts/*.sh`.
  A failed attempt triggers an Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`, effort high) repair job
  that reads the failed log, fixes the checked-out tree, and pushes to the
  repair branch (nightly candidate / dispatched branch); the next attempt
  builds that exact sha so every deterministic gate re-runs. Max 3 attempts /
  2 repairs, then fail loud. Repairs may never change the app version or touch
  `FEATURES.md` (`scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` gates marker survival).
- **Nightly merge.** `.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml` (02:13 UTC): when
  upstream publishes a newer `desktop-v*` tag, git merges it; Opus 5 resolves
  conflicted files, then a `(MERGE-ADAPT)` proactive port pass adapts fork-only
  callers to cleanly-merging upstream API refactors. Deterministic gates follow
  (FEATURES.md marker survival, dependency/lock consistency, `(REFERR-GATE)`
  cannot-find-name check), then a bounded `(MERGE-SEMANTIC-GATE)` review →
  adapt → fresh-review loop (max 3 reviews / 2 repairs). Green all the way =
  build (with its own repair loop), publish the Release, advance the baseline
  to the BUILT sha; ANY unrepaired failure hard-aborts with the baseline
  untouched → fix locally with the maintainer and re-baseline. A
  `rehearse=true` dispatch replays a night's merge half with zero side effects.
  A night blocked ONLY by a PROVEN `(AI-UNAVAILABLE)` abort (declared by the
  wrapper, never an exit code alone) merged, built and published nothing, so it
  concludes GREEN (no email) as a loud no-op with build/advance skipped — until
  `AI_UNAVAILABLE_STREAK_THRESHOLD` (7, owned by the script) consecutive blocked
  NIGHTS, which fails RED. Same-day re-runs count once, and only a night where
  the CLI provably reached the model clears the streak.
- **Key files.** `FEATURES.md` (feature manifest + fenced `markers` block the
  gates parse), `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt`,
  `scripts/check-dangerous-diagnostics.mjs` (REFERR gate),
  `scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` (standalone marker gate),
  `scripts/ci-repair.sh` (build-repair engine),
  `scripts/ai-run.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) classification + shared Claude CLI wrapper),
  `scripts/ai-streak.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) green no-op + consecutive-blocked-night
  escalation),
  `scripts/check-override-consistency.mjs`, `scripts/resolve-release-age.mjs`,
  companion native packages `github.com/khairm/libsql-windows-arm64` +
  `github.com/khairm/tokenizers-windows-arm64`.

## Non-negotiables

- **Whole feature set or fail loud** — every `FEATURES.md` marker survives a
  merge or the run aborts; never ship a partial fork.
- **v2-only, forever** — the v2 cloud/host-service stack is pinned on; never v1.
- **No phone-home to upstream (phase 1)** — upstream's telemetry, auto-update
  and desktop-notice channels are deliberately SEVERED as of cloud severance
  phase 1 (`(CLOUD-SEVERANCE-P1)`, `(EGRESS-FENCE)`): dead PostHog/Sentry keys,
  a no-op CLI analytics call, a disabled updater and a notices poll that fetches
  nothing are the intended state, not breakage to repair. Sign-in, Electric and
  the api.superset.sh data plane are still live and are phase 2/3.
- **One version, ever** — exactly one Release per upstream version, tagged
  `desktop-v<version>`, rebuilt in place; no betas/prereleases.
- **No build-time type/test gate except `(REFERR-GATE)`** — the tree carries
  accepted type debt; only cannot-find-name diagnostics fail the build.
  Validate + e2e locally before relying on a release.
- **Everything is AI-touchable** (needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`): the nightly
  merge resolves/ports/reviews, and the build self-repairs via `(BUILD-REPAIR)`.
  Workflow YAML self-repair additionally needs the `WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN` secret
  (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and only takes effect the NEXT
  run — workflow files are frozen once a run starts, which is why all step
  logic lives in `.github/actions/` + `scripts/` (repairable mid-run).
  Rate-limited/unparsable AI output aborts rather than ships.

## Custom features / overrides

`FEATURES.md` is the authoritative manifest (descriptions + marker tokens).
In brief:

- **Native Windows ARM64 packaging** — one-click installer; ARM64 node-pty,
  libsql, tokenizers; renderer CORS for `superset-app://`.
- **Window controls** — native `titleBarOverlay` is the sole min/max/close on
  Windows, theme-matched; upstream's duplicates hidden.
- **Windows behaviour fixes** — skip quit-confirm; cmd.exe fallback;
  force-foreground; hidden-window watchdog; WebGL first-paint recovery; Wispr
  Flow accessibility/paste fix; fast non-blocking startup.
- **Agent status dots (Claude + Codex)** — per-terminal + workspace-rollup dot:
  red = needs input, yellow = working (incl. subagents/teammates/compaction/
  codex-companion holds), green = ready for review, blue = shell/background/
  cloud activity; precedence red > yellow > blue > green. All surfaces (tab,
  pane header, sidebar row + agent chips, rollup, kanban card) derive from one
  per-source primitive with independent latched axes; hook-driven via
  `superset-notify.py` POSTs with self-healing markers and persistence across
  renderer reloads; companion phone/watch alerts cover blocked questions,
  ready-for-review, and terminal-agent failures.
- **Auto-resume** — after an API failure, idle Claude terminals re-send
  automatically (bounded retries/budget, default-on, away-detection).
- **Recycle Bin** — every delete entry point soft-deletes (30-day display
  window); permanent delete only from inside the bin.
- **Non-git / multi-repo workspaces** — open any folder (non-git or multi-repo)
  as a plain workspace.
- **Multi-repo branch workspaces** — group N git repos under one project row;
  its "+" fans a branch out as worktrees per member (all-or-nothing, adoption
  on resume, editable membership, loud partial-state failures).
- **Workspace branch label** — branch name top-right in the tab bar; click
  copies.
- **Thread snooze / archive** — timed Snooze (auto-returns) + sticky Archive in
  revealable sidebar sections.
- **Sidebar** — pinned > active > idle tier sort with stable manual drag order;
  hover freezes re-sorting.
- **Terminal links** — plain click copies a URL/path; Ctrl/Cmd+click opens.
- **Agent-hook bash-wrap** — Gemini/Cursor `.sh` hooks run via Git-for-Windows
  bash.
- **Kanban board** — device-local board of every sidebar project's branches +
  Queued and final Completed columns, custom columns, deadlines, per-column
  date filters, promote-to-branch drag, sidebar Mark completed for active
  worktrees, frozen completed records, append-only daily JSON backups under
  `~/.superset/backups/kanban/`.

## Live footguns (do NOT repeat)

- No synchronous/blocking fs on the main thread at startup — the renderer's
  `superset-app://` loader starves and the window stays blank for minutes.
- Never re-enable xterm `screenReaderMode` (Wispr Flow regression); the build
  hard-fails if it is truthy in a renderer bundle.
- Never let `ws` load native bufferutil/utf-8-validate in the host-service —
  keep `WS_NO_BUFFER_UTIL=1` + `WS_NO_UTF_8_VALIDATE=1` in the coordinator
  child env AND first-import in serve.ts.
- Keep agent-hook `.sh` templates pipeline-free (bash builtins only) —
  subprocess-fork cascades crash emulated msys2 on ARM64 (`(HOOK-FORK-DIET)`).
- `.github/workflows` is fork-owned and CI's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can never push
  workflow changes — nightly-merge restores the dir mid-merge
  (`(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)`); add upstream workflows only by deliberate local
  commit with a user token. `(BUILD-REPAIR)` pushes that touch workflow files
  use `WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN` (also the advance job's push credential, since a
  repaired candidate may carry workflow commits into main).
- Never assert upstream-derived incidental names (Rollup chunk filenames, file
  hashes, ordering) in fork-owned gates — assert the invariant over the whole
  artifact set (`SCREENREADER-GUARD-DRIFT`: a chunk rename blocked 3 nightlies).

## Accepted limitations

Unsigned installer (SmartScreen warns); no full type/test gate (type debt is
accepted, `(REFERR-GATE)` only); an unattended nightly can publish a Release —
the gate stack shrinks but does not eliminate the
semantically-wrong-but-compiling window, so e2e-test before relying on one.
`(BUILD-REPAIR)` widens that window: an unattended repair agent can push code
that passes every deterministic gate yet is semantically wrong or (via
prompt-injected build logs) malicious — containment is credential-less agent
steps, trusted-blob validation, version/FEATURES.md freezes, and tip-pinning,
not semantic review. A direct build dispatch racing a just-started nightly
fails that nightly loudly (non-ff advance) and self-heals next night. Repair
commits on a nightly candidate do NOT persist across nights: an aborted
nightly's candidate is deleted and re-derived next run, so a break needing
more than 2 repairs re-derives them from zero each night until fixed locally.
Gate scripts are frozen against repair edits — a genuine bug in a gate script
is deliberately NOT self-repairable (fail loud, maintainer fixes).

```
        ├── HeroSection.test.tsx           # Tests co-located
        ├── index.ts
        └── components/                    # Used ONLY by HeroSection
            └── HeroCanvas/
                ├── HeroCanvas.tsx
                ├── HeroCanvas.test.tsx
                ├── HeroCanvas.stories.tsx
                ├── index.ts
                └── config.ts

components/                                # Used in 2+ pages (last resort)
└── Header/
```

1. **One folder per component**: `ComponentName/ComponentName.tsx` + `index.ts` for barrel export
2. **Co-locate by usage**: If used once, nest under parent's `components/`. If used 2+ times, promote to **highest shared parent's** `components/` (or `components/` as last resort)
3. **One component per file**: No multi-component files
4. **Co-locate dependencies**: Utils, hooks, constants, config, tests, stories live next to the file using them

### Exception: shadcn/ui Components

The `src/components/ui/` and `src/components/ai-elements` directories contain shadcn/ui components. These use **kebab-case single files** (e.g., `button.tsx`, `base-node.tsx`) instead of the folder structure above. This is intentional—shadcn CLI expects this format for updates via `bunx shadcn@latest add`.

## Database

Drizzle ORM, schema in `packages/db/src/`. Follow `.agents/skills/db-migrations/SKILL.md` to generate
migrations. Never hand-edit `packages/db/drizzle/` (SQL, `meta/_journal.json`, snapshots) without
explicit user confirmation, and never apply migrations against a shared or production database.

## Releases

Desktop, host-service, and cli share one version; cut releases on a dedicated branch. Runbook:
`scripts/release/README.md`. A *canary* is a separate thing: `bash scripts/release-canary.sh
[commit]` builds the rolling internal `desktop-canary` prerelease, not a versioned release.

## Orchestrating agents and workspaces

When work wants a fresh isolated environment, a parallel agent, or a long-running job, reach for the
`superset` CLI instead of hand-rolling git worktrees or doing it all serially in this one. It's
already on `PATH` in Superset terminals, and we dogfood it.

Replace the capitalized placeholders before running these:

```bash
superset ws create --project PROJECT_ID --branch BRANCH --agent claude --prompt "..."
superset agents create --workspace WORKSPACE_ID --agent claude --prompt "..."
superset ws list
superset terminals read --workspace WORKSPACE_ID --terminal TERMINAL_ID
superset ws delete WORKSPACE_ID
```

In order: an isolated workspace with an agent already working in it, another agent in an existing
workspace, what's running, what an agent is doing right now, and cleanup when you're done.

`superset <command> --help` covers the rest (tasks, automations, hosts, settings). Pass `--json` for
parsable output; it's on by default under agent environments.

## Further reading

- `.agents/skills/`: CDP UI verification, DB migrations, ticket format, and more. Read the matching
  `SKILL.md` when a task fits its description.
- `docs/agent-tooling.md`: where commands, skills, and per-agent-CLI config live.
- `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md`: desktop specifics (notices, persisted renderer state).
- `apps/mobile/AGENTS.md`: mobile structure and iOS-only scope.
- `docs/cloud-sandbox-mismatches.md`: where cloud workspace sandboxes don't fit assumptions the
  app makes about a machine someone owns. Read it before touching sandboxes, and add to it when
  you find a new one.
- `docs/cloud-sandbox-considerations.md`: what cloud sandboxes still owe before they leave the
  team — billing, credential blast radius, untested behaviour.

skills.content:
Review target: `apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.ts apps/desktop/src/main/lib/agent-jsonl-watcher/pane-map-hook.test.ts`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

content.content: @AGENTS.md

## Server-driven announcements (desktop notices)

To show an announcement/warning popup in the app without shipping a release, insert a row in the `desktop_notices` table (served by `GET /api/desktop/version`). Authoring guide — markdown-only body, severities, triggers, targeting, QA previews: `docs/DESKTOP_NOTICES.md`.

## Persisted renderer state (localStorage) policy

Renderer localStorage has one ~10 MB quota, loads synchronously at boot, and keys outlive the code that wrote them — unbounded growth has frozen the renderer before (23.7 MB profile, GH #5496). Every writer must be allowlisted in `src/renderer/lib/persisted-keys/persisted-key-registry.test-data.ts` (CI fails on unregistered writers), and code review must answer three questions:

1. **What bounds it?** A cap/LRU, a TTL, reconciliation against an owning entity, or "fixed-size singleton". "It's small per write" is not a bound.
2. **Who deletes it?** New entity-keyed data belongs in SQLite; existing stores must document their deletion path or sunset plan because deletes from CLIs or other machines can bypass UI cleanup. One-shot payloads must be cleared by their consumer. Deleting a map entry means removing the key, never writing `null`.
3. **What happens when the feature dies?** Move the keys to `DEAD_KEYS` in the same PR that removes the writer; the boot sweep cleans existing profiles. Deleting the writer without registering the key strands it on user profiles forever.

Guardrail: localStorage is for small singleton UI state. Anything entity-scoped with unbounded cardinality, or payloads beyond a few KB, belongs in host-side SQLite (`@superset/local-db` schema, reached over `electronTrpc`) — localStorage collections re-serialize the whole org blob on every mutation. Since #6328 removed SQLite-backed collection persistence, every TanStack DB collection in `CollectionsProvider` is localStorage-backed, so the ~10 MB quota is shared by all of them; `withQuotaGuard`, `notifyQuotaExhausted`, and `evictInactiveOrgs` exist to absorb that pressure and are not a licence to store more.

## Verifying renderer changes via CDP

Read `.agents/skills/cdp-verification/SKILL.md`: attaching to the right renderer, repairing auth, and what counts as end-to-end evidence.

name: Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)

# Self-repairing build of the vendored fork source at repo root.
# The build steps themselves are deterministic and live in
# .github/actions/arm64-build (thin shims over scripts/) — this file only
# orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop:
#
#   build-attempt-1 ──fail──> repair-1 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-2
#                                   ──fail──> repair-2 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-3
#
# Max 3 build attempts / 2 AI repairs, then verdict fails LOUD. Every repair
# is pushed to the repair branch (nightly candidate, or the dispatched branch
# for manual runs) and the next attempt builds that exact sha, so every
# deterministic gate re-runs on the repaired tree. (BUILD-REPAIR)
#
# Why the split matters: workflow YAML is frozen when a run starts and
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push .github/workflows changes — but .github/actions/**
# and scripts/** are ordinary repo files, checked out per attempt, so the
# repair AI can fix ~everything mid-run. Workflow-YAML fixes need the
# WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and
# take effect the NEXT run.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: 'Publish the desktop-v<version> Release (rebuilt in place; one version, no beta)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (default: the dispatched branch)'
        type: string
        default: ''
  # Reusable so nightly-merge.yml can invoke the exact same build.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      publish:
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build (default: the triggering ref)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (nightly passes the candidate)'
        type: string
        default: ''
    outputs:
      built_sha:
        description: 'The exact commit the successful attempt built (differs from the input ref when a repair landed)'
        value: ${{ jobs.verdict.outputs.built_sha }}

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: read # repair jobs download this run's failed-job logs

jobs:
  build-attempt-1:
    runs-on: windows-11-arm
    timeout-minutes: 180
    # Failures are handled by the repair loop; verdict is the single source of
    # truth for the workflow result. (Job-level continue-on-error masks the
    # failure in `needs.*.result`, so the loop keys off the `ok` OUTPUT — only
    # a fully green attempt sets it.)
    continue-on-error: true
    outputs:
      ok: ${{ steps.done.outputs.ok }}
      sha: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      # Superset has paths deeper than Windows' 260-char MAX_PATH; without this
      # actions/checkout dies with "Filename too long". Must run BEFORE
      # checkout, so it cannot live in the composite action.
      - name: Configure git long paths (Windows MAX_PATH)
        shell: bash
        run: git config --system core.longpaths true || git config --global core.longpaths true
      # A direct dispatch's repair loop pushes to a live branch; racing a
      # nightly's candidate/advance would fail that nightly loudly (non-ff) —
      # refuse up front instead. Only guards direct dispatches: when called
      # from nightly-merge, github.workflow is the CALLER's name.
      - name: Direct-dispatch mutex — refuse while a nightly is active
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.workflow == 'Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ACTIVE=$(gh run list --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --workflow nightly-merge.yml --limit 50 --json databaseId,status --jq '[.[] | select(.status=="in_progress" or .status=="queued" or .status=="waiting" or .status=="requested" or .status=="pending")] | length')
          if [ "$ACTIVE" != "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::(BUILD-REPAIR) a nightly-merge run is in progress/queued — a direct build's repairs could race its candidate/advance. Retry after it finishes."
            exit 1

<result>Re-reviewed the current files (both changed since my first pass: 821 vs 753 insertions).

**My previous MAJOR is fixed.** `pane-map-hook.ts:1613` now reads `if entry_id in previously_seen: continue` with no `migrating_v5` bypass, and `migrating_v5` is confined to lines 1469/1516/1546/1563/1565 (the historical replay only). Verified in-memory that the shape that produced the double-spend is now unreachable through the exact binder.

Verification of each requested area, all re-run against the current file by extracting the embedded Python and exec'ing it in memory (read-only, no files written):

1. **Startup/clear fresh boundary** — `_team_initialize_fresh_cache` (1401) locks, snapshots `stat().st_size` as `offset`, writes an empty v6 record. Called only from `main()` at 3206 under `source in ("startup","clear")`. Pre-existing transcript bytes become historical; post-boundary spawns are causal. Failure to stat or lock writes nothing → next Stop is cold → `loaded_cache=False` → no exact trust. Clean.
2. **Resume/compact preservation** — those sources never reach 3206, and neither event is `Stop`/`SubagentStop`, so no ledger run and no cache mutation. A compaction that shrinks the transcript trips `offset > size` (1552) → full reset → cold path. Clean.
3. **Cache-loss safe yellow** — corrupt/missing cache → `except` at 1535 resets to `_team_empty_ledger()` and `loaded_cache=False`; the exact-trust block at 1608 is gated on `loaded_cache`. Verified: untrusted exact row yields `candidates=[]` → not droppable. Clean.
4. **Cold exact trust gate** — `if not partial_tail and loaded_cache:`. Verified `A(entry, mk, idx, {'r1':['w']}, set())` → `candidates=[]`, `droppable=False`; trusted+bound → `True`; trusted but binding lost → `False`. Clean.
5. **v5 prompt chronology** — `match_keys = {...} if offset == 0 else {}` (1523-1530). With `offset>0` the seed is dropped so the historical replay rebuilds `prompts` in document order; seeding first would leave the newest prompt at index 0 and make `prompts[-1:]` (the unbound latest-only rule at 1745) pick a stale prompt. Verified the rule itself: unbound row against `['Old…','New…']` → `candidates=[]`; causally bound row → `['w']`. Clean.
6. **Previously-seen v5 no-rebind** — line 1613, unconditional. Clean.
7. **Mixed exact+legacy spawn budget** — `len(first_seen_ids) <= len(spawns)` at 1719 with `first_seen_ids` (1711) counting exact-bound rows. Also confirmed the supporting invariant: `_team_bind_entries` returns `stale[-192:] + [live ids]`, and `bound` keys are always live, so persisted `entryNames ⊆ seenIds` — therefore the only first-seen rows in `bound` are this run's exact binds and the budget accounting is exact. Verified: `bind({'tEXACT':['known']},['tOLDER'],['tEXACT','tLEGACY'],['known'])` → `{'tEXACT': ['known']}`, tLEGACY unbound. `single`, `two_two`, `three_two`, `reseen`, `empty_spawns` all unchanged from pre-fix behavior.
8. **Stale-writer lock** — `_team_cache_lock` (1306) holds an exclusive byte lock across the whole read/scan/bind/write transaction for both the ledger and the fresh init; `_team_ledger` discards its result when `_team_cache_unlock` reports failure; acquisition failure or the 2s deadline returns `None` → raw `bg_tasks` → yellow. `msvcrt` contention surfaces as `EDEADLK`, which is in the retry set. `_team_write_cache` writes a pid-suffixed temp then `os.replace`, inside the lock. Clean.

One remaining item, reported as a tradeoff rather than a bug:

```
[MINOR] C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\.claude\worktrees\agent-a09b13f5e51060a85\apps\desktop\src\main\lib\agent-jsonl-watcher\pane-map-hook.ts:1740

Fix: If you want a bounded escape, fall through to the legacy prompt-prefix bucket when `exact_names` is non-empty but the row is untrusted (the bucket still requires every matching name idle). If permanent yellow is the intended tradeoff, say so in the comment at 1740 so the next reader does not "fix" it.
```
